claims.head: The Avalanche should tilt the ice
claims.body: The Avalanche have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Blackhawks one of the worst. Expect the Avalanche to spend more of the night in the Blackhawks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

story.head: The Avalanche should tilt the ice
paras: The Avalanche (7-5-1) beat New Jersey 5-2 on Wednesday, while the Blackhawks (4-9-0) lost 4-1 to Detroit on Thursday. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Avalanche third (tied for 16th in the NHL) and the Blackhawks last (31st).

The Avalanche’s record (.577) is about what their chances are worth. The Blackhawks have played better than their record (.308) says: their chances are worth about .368, and their finishing has held them back.

The Avalanche (lowest) and the Blackhawks (2nd lowest) both do a lot of their shooting from distance. The Avalanche play the league’s fastest games (1st) and get their defensemen shooting (2nd). Colorado has scored 4.15 goals a game, the second most in the league. The Blackhawks don't block many shots (32nd). They also have struggled on the power play (32nd), so their struggling power play gets a tough test from the Avalanche’s penalty killers. Chicago has scored 2.08 goals a game, the second fewest in the league, and allowed 3.69, the fourth most. The Avs are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Blackhawks.

Nathan MacKinnon (8 G / 14 A / 22 P in 13 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring and is tied for fifth in the NHL. Artturi Lehkonen (10 G / 5 A / 15 P in 13 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for fourth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. For the Blackhawks, Patrick Kane (1 G / 7 A / 8 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Roman Kantserov (5 G / 1 A / 6 P in 13 GP) has a team-high five goals.
Mackenzie Blackwood (6-3-0 / .894 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for Colorado, and Spencer Knight (4-7-0 / .897 SV% in 11 GS) for Chicago.
The Avalanche usually control more of the chances than the Blackhawks do.
